questions.sec: IgG4 Biology, Pathology & Core Clinical Profile
questions.q: Which condition heads the IgG4-related-disease spectrum as the most common manifestation on the next page?
questions.exp: The spectrum lists type 1 autoimmune pancreatitis, Mikulicz disease, Riedel thyroiditis, mediastinal fibrosis, primary sclerosing cholangitis and periaortitis; p450 calls type 1 AIP the most common manifestation. (Book p449)

questions.sec: IgG4 Biology, Pathology & Core Clinical Profile
questions.q: How is IgG4 characterised among IgG subclasses in the source?
questions.exp: IgG4 is listed as least common (<5%). (Book p449)

questions.sec: IgG4 Biology, Pathology & Core Clinical Profile
questions.q: Which functional property of IgG4 is specifically stated?
opts: It is the principal opsonin for bacteria
questions.exp: IgG4 is anti-inflammatory, blocks IgG–C1q binding, does not fix complement, and is a bispecific antibody with two antigen-binding sites that binds/sequesters antigen. (Book p449)

questions.sec: IgG4 Biology, Pathology & Core Clinical Profile
questions.q: A biopsy shows tumefactive plasma-cell-rich inflammation, storiform fibrosis and obliterative phlebitis. What disease is most strongly suggested?
questions.exp: Histology lists IgG4-predominant lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, tumour-like lesions, storiform fibrosis, obliterative phlebitis and mild eosinophilia. (Book p449)

questions.sec: IgG4 Biology, Pathology & Core Clinical Profile
questions.q: Which cytokine is called the most potent fibrogenic cytokine in the pathogenesis flowchart?
questions.exp: Antigenic stimuli → IgG4 plasma-lymphocytic infiltrate → myofibroblast activation → TGF-β/PDGF → fibrosis; TGF-β is called most potent fibrogenic cytokine. (Book p449)

questions.sec: IgG4 Biology, Pathology & Core Clinical Profile
questions.q: Obliterative phlebitis is noted as occurring in IgG4-related disease and which other disease?
questions.exp: The page's note pairs obliterative phlebitis with IgG4-related disease and Behcet disease. (Book p449)

questions.sec: IgG4 Biology, Pathology & Core Clinical Profile
questions.q: Which demographic pattern is given for IgG4-related disease?
opts: Men more than women, age 40–70, subacute onset
Women more than men, childhood onset
questions.exp: Clinical features: M>F, age 40–70 years, subacute onset; symptoms weight loss and myalgia. (Book p449)

questions.sec: IgG4 Biology, Pathology & Core Clinical Profile
questions.q: Which finding is listed as arguing against IgG4-related disease?
questions.exp: Features against IgG4-RD: fever, arthritis, neutrophil involvement and granuloma. Mild eosinophilia appears among histology/atopy-allergy history. (Book p449)

questions.q: A patient has obstructive jaundice, diffuse irregular pancreatic-duct narrowing on ERCP, and a ‘sausage pancreas’ with homogeneous enhancement on CT. What manifestation is most likely?
questions.exp: Type 1 autoimmune pancreatitis is most common in IgG4-RD and presents with obstructive jaundice; ERCP is IOC and CT shows sausage pancreas/homogeneous enhancement. (Book p450)

questions.q: Type 1 autoimmune pancreatitis can be associated with which endocrine and exocrine consequences?
questions.exp: AIP is associated with endocrine insufficiency → type 3c DM and exocrine insufficiency → malabsorption. (Book p450)

questions.q: A patient has bilateral painless submandibular enlargement but minimal sicca symptoms. Which IgG4 manifestation is represented?
questions.exp: Salivary involvement is bilateral painless submandibular enlargement with minimal sicca symptoms. (Book p450)

questions.q: What is the most common orbital manifestation of IgG4-related disease on the page?
questions.exp: Orbital/periorbital lesions include orbital inflammatory pseudotumours; lacrimal enlargement/dacryoadenitis is marked most common orbital manifestation. (Book p450)

questions.q: Which CNS manifestation is specified in postpartum women with raised intracranial tension?
questions.exp: Minor CNS manifestations are lymphocytic hypophysitis (postpartum women with ↑ICT) and pachymeningitis without parenchymal involvement. (Book p450)

questions.q: What is the most common renal manifestation of IgG4-related disease?
questions.exp: Tubulointerstitial disease is most common renal manifestation, with minimal CKD risk and no renal tubular acidosis; membranous nephropathy is glomerular involvement. (Book p450)

questions.q: Which bile-duct manifestation is listed under IgG4-related disease?
questions.exp: The organ list continues with bile duct: primary sclerosing cholangitis. (Book p451)

questions.q: Which lung finding is described for IgG4-related disease?
opts: NSIP with thickening of the bronchovascular bundle
LIP with cysts as the defining pattern
questions.exp: Lung: non-specific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) and thickening of bronchovascular bundle. (Book p451)

questions.q: Which vascular manifestation may be associated with a paravertebral mass?
questions.exp: Aorta manifestation is periaortitis, associated with paravertebral mass. (Book p451)

questions.q: A patient has membranous nephropathy as an IgG4 manifestation. What complement pattern is noted?
questions.exp: The page notes membranonephropathy manifestation of IgG4 disease → low complements. (Book p451)

questions.q: What three domains compose the RCD 2020 criteria as shown?
opts: Pathologic findings, serology and clinical features
questions.exp: RCD 2020 criteria show pathologic/histologic features + serology + clinical features; serum IgG4 correlates with activity and is elevated in 40% cases. (Book p451)

questions.q: Which ratio is stated to be a better marker than serum IgG4 alone?
questions.exp: Other findings: IgG4/IgG ratio is a better marker. (Book p451)

questions.q: Mikulicz disease involves enlargement of which glands?
questions.exp: Mikulicz disease is enlargement of parotid, submandibular and lacrimal gland; history includes chronic sinusitis/nasal obstruction with eosinophilia. (Book p451)

questions.q: What first-line treatment and relapse-prevention steroid-sparing agent are listed for IgG4-related disease?
opts: Steroids first line; rituximab to prevent relapse
NSAIDs first line; IVIG for relapse
questions.exp: Steroids are first line with good response within two weeks but relapse risk; rituximab is the steroid-sparing agent to prevent relapse. (Book p451)

questions.q: A patient has pronounced salivary enlargement, little sicca, and good steroid response but relapse risk. Which diagnosis is favoured over Sjogren in the comparison table?
questions.exp: Comparison: IgG4 has increased salivary enlargement, decreased sicca, good steroid response and relapse risk; Sjogren has decreased enlargement, increased sicca and sicca symptoms not steroid responsive. (Book p451)

units.title: 1. IgG4 Biology, Pathology & Core Clinical Profile
units.sec: IgG4 Biology, Pathology & Core Clinical Profile
units.guide:
IgG4’s unusual immunobiology is paired with its fibro-inflammatory pathology.
The disease spectrum and histological signature precede the demographic profile.
Negative clues are included to distinguish mimics.

units.title: 2. Organ Manifestations, Diagnosis & Treatment
units.guide:
Autoimmune pancreatitis is tied to imaging and endocrine/exocrine consequences.
Salivary, orbital, CNS, renal, biliary, pulmonary and aortic disease follow in sequence.
RCD criteria and treatment are contrasted directly with Sjogren syndrome.
